title: Inference Slots — playbook + quick sketch
content:
Top-level idea: expose a small set of "inference slots" (developer-defined tiers) to end-users and to internal feature flags so product teams can offer deterministic tradeoffs: latency vs cost vs quality.

Why: customers keep asking for predictable UX knobs ("make it faster but cheaper"). We have a lot of back-end levers (batching, quant, routing, cache) but no simple surface for app teams to expose to users or to bind to UI affordances, paywall tiers, or A/B experiments.

Core concept: an "inference slot" is a named profile (fast, balanced, thrifty, long-context, hallucination-guarded) that maps to a small bundle of runtime routing + model variant + quantization + batching hints + SLOs. Slots are first-class objects in the API and Console, editable by product owners.

Notes / rough bullets:
- Slots are not just pricing tiers — they're runtime contracts (soft SLOs) + config presets.
- Each slot = {model_variant, region_hint, routing_policy, batching_priority, cache_policy, quant_profile, fallback_slot}. (We don't need a new schema now; just keep as mapping)
- Default dev surface: 3 slots: Fast (low latency, higher cost), Balanced (default), Thrifty (low cost, higher latency, compressed model). Add Experimental slots for A/B.
- Slots carry an optional "upgrade flow": on slow/failed responses, app can surface a one-tap upgrade that retries on a higher slot. Good for upsells.
- UI: small segment control in client SDK: {slot: "balanced"}. Console: visual editor, preview RT/UnitCost estimate.

Example user stories:
- As an app product manager, I want to create a "Fast" slot that pins GPT-like-7b-int8, routes to eu-west-1, and disables batching for <50ms p50, so I can offer realtime assistant in the pro tier. Acceptance: console shows expected latency/cost; flag created; SDK accepts slot parameter and runtime honors it.
- As frontend, I want to show a "Make response faster (+$0.03)" CTA when we hit a slow p95 so users can pay for an upgrade without losing context. Acceptance: CTA triggers server-side retry on new slot and preserves session state.
- As platform, I want telemetry per-slot: token counts, p50/p95/p99, fallback rate, upgrade conversions. Acceptance: dashboards expose per-slot metrics, and alert if fallback_rate > 5%.

API ideas (sketch):
- request param: inference_slot="fast" (string) or slot_id.
- create slot: POST /slots {name, model_variant, quant_profile, routing_constraint, cost_estimate_meta, fallback_slot}
- SDKs add convenience helpers: Redwood.slots.list(), Redwood.slots.getActive(), Redwood.request({slot: "thrifty"})

Operational constraints / safety:
- Reserved slots should be limited for Dedicated customers to avoid noisy neighbors. For hosted, slots can be soft-policies with graceful fallback.
- Default slot must exist per-API-key. If slot not found, fallback to default routing.
- Billing: map slot to a multiplier or explicit pricing; need cross-team input (billing) on how we expose per-request delta versus model-priced tokens.

Experiment plan / rollout:
- Phase 0: invisible to end-users — console + API only. Allow internal apps to opt-in (eng teams). Collect telemetry.
- Phase 1: small set of Redwood internal apps surface slot selector in UI (helpdesk, console). Test upgrade CTA flow.
- Phase 2: public beta — SDK flag to enable slot param; docs + quickstart; one-month A/B.

Telemetry and evals:
- Track per-slot quality regressions with eval harness (use our eval prompt-set to compare Balanced->Thrifty). If quality drop > X% reject.
- Add slot-level canary: initially small traff to new slot, auto rollback on error spikes.

Open questions / hazards:
- How to represent stateful session migration when upgrading mid-request? E.g., KV cache/kv prefix differences between model variants. Need migration guidelines.
- Pricing model: commit-level vs per-request delta vs subscription add-on. Which sells? (ask GTM)
- UX: Upsell interrupts are annoying. Need microcopy experiment and conversion tracking.
- Security: custom slots could encourage customers to create heavy-weight slots and DOS the system. Need policy + quotas.

Implementation rough work breakdown (me + Maya + SRE):
- Backend: slot schema, routing hook, slot evaluation pipeline (2 sprints).
- Console: slot editor + cost preview (1 sprint).
- SDK: slot param and client helpers + example (1 sprint).
- Telemetry: per-slot metrics in Console + alerts (1 sprint).

Short-term next steps (TODO):
- Draft a simple slot schema and wireframe in Figma (assigned to Maya).
- Post initial JIRA (JIRA-INF-7892) with endpoints and telemetry metrics (Imran).
- Quick internal demo to SRE and Billing to validate quotas and pricing approach (Noah).
- Set up lightweight eval: create 10 prompts that are sensitive to quantization and compare Balanced vs Thrifty (Research).

Notes to self / fragments:
- Could combine with Optimize's recommendations: "suggest slot X for prompt Y". Automatic slot suggestion based on prompt length and intent detection.
- Maybe integrate with rollouts: slot can be targeted by percentage, user segments. Use existing rollout infra.
- Consider UI for multi-slot composition: block-level slots (e.g., prompt preface runs in Thrifty, generation runs in Fast). Fancy but later.

Links / references:
- Slack thread: #prod-inference "slot concept" (search: "inference slot")
- Related quick wins: expose simple "response preference" in SDK (low effort).

Bottom line: this is a developer-friendly way to make our runtime levers consumable by product teams and users. Low-ish infra risk if we treat as soft policy first. Good candidate for a beta feature tied to Optimize recommendations and Console tooling.

-- end of sketch --

Quick action: rename to "inference-slot-playbook" when we stabilize and split into PRD + UI spec + API doc.
